runs.question: Under Northbridge University's guidance, may faculty enter Level 2 research data into the university's approved AI assistant?

answer.text:
The documents conflict, and nothing in them says which one governs, so I can't give a clean yes.

**The IT standard permits it.** The Office of Information Technology's standard names Northbridge AI as the approved tool. Northbridge AI, the university's enterprise generative AI assistant, is the approved tool for university work. Under that standard, the answer is yes for Level 2 data: faculty, staff and researchers may enter data classified up to Level 2 (Moderate Risk), including unpublished research data, into Northbridge AI.

**The research guidance prohibits it.** The Office of Research's guidance takes a stricter line. It says that research data classified above Level 1 (Public) must not be entered into any generative AI tool, including university-licensed tools. Its stated reason is that sponsor agreements and data use agreements often restrict where data may be processed. It adds that generative AI services may log prompts outside the systems those agreements cover.

**Why I can't settle it from the documents.** Both documents are effective September 1, 2026 and apply university-wide to faculty, staff and researchers. Neither refers to the other, and neither says it overrides the other. The guidance is the only one that addresses research data specifically, and its restriction covers university-licensed tools, so it would bar Level 2 research data from Northbridge AI. Reading the two together, the more cautious course is to keep Level 2 research data out of Northbridge AI until the conflict is resolved.

Also, both documents are marked "SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT," so confirm that they are the current official versions before relying on them.

To get a definitive answer, ask the Office of Research Compliance (the guidance's contact) or the IT Service Desk (the standard's contact) which document governs Level 2 research data.
